newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares firm 0.59 pct to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares firm 0.59 pct to new record.

text.p: Istanbul shares firmed amid selective trade led by shares of largely state-owned bluechip firms on Monday, with the market index continuing this year's string of records, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed at an all-time high of 1,201, up seven points, or 0.59 percent from Friday's previous record of 1,194. But in dollar terms, it eased to 1.05 cents from Friday's 1.06-cent record as the lira weakened sharply against the dollar.
Daily trade volume fell to 19.26 trillion lira ($168.7 million) from Friday's 22.96 trillion ($203.5 million).

Brokers said demand in shares of largely state-owned firms were boosted by renewed privatisation hopes in the afternoon following the completion of negotiations in the sell-off tender of public Etibank at midday.

"The market rose on state shares, namely (flat steel maker) Eregli in the afternoon amid positive privatisation expectations buoyed by related comments and the finalisation of the Etibank tender," said Mustafa Karaahmetoglu from Sayilgan securities.
Eregli has a strong impact on the market index due to its large market capitalisation.

State Minister Ufuk Soylemez said after the Etibank negotiations were completed that Turkey would reach its target of $5 billion in privatisation revenues this year if there were no legal obstacles to sell-offs.
He also said the target did not include $3.5 billion expected to be raised from the sale of Turk Telekom, the centrepiece of the government's privatisation efforts.

The stock market awaits a constitutional court ruling tomorrow on a law designed to enable Telekom's sell-off. A legal adviser to the privatisation agency OIB said last Thursday he feared the court would cancel the law.
The market index has surged 23.05 percent, breaking 12 record closes since the beginning of 1997.
